nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: Wait. Something here is not quite right.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: The notices are pinned at the same height except one, which sits higher. The tape behind it is still clean. Someone moved it up to be read - who, and why, is more than I can tell from this.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: A board with a few sheets pinned to it. What else is there to see?

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You read the top two: a room wanted, a piano for sale. The third has been turned face-in. It has not been taken down.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: The yard is long and fairly narrow. The path comes in at one corner.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: There is a seam down the middle of the concrete, where two pours meet, running the length of it. But the gate is on the short side. What is wrong I cannot name. I can only say the shape and the way in do not agree.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: A yard. Two hoops, a shed, a bench.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You have seen a yard like this before. Or perhaps schoolyards just tend to look alike.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: Hold on. Look at where the hoop's pole is set.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: The concrete around the pole is newer than the rest of the yard, and there are old bolt holes in the wall, filled and painted over. The hoop was somewhere else before - or only the pole was replaced. I cannot tell which.

nodes.speaker: voice_orientation
nodes.text: The rim looks to be at an ordinary height.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You couldn't say how high a hoop is meant to be. But the concrete around the base is a different colour, and the net looks newer than the rim.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: I have seen this water stain before. Not on this planter - on another wall, higher up.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: Someone poured water at the same spot every day then. Said it kept the insects off. I cannot remember who.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: You crouch and compare it against its shadow. The bottom edge is older than the moss at the wall's foot. The edge itself is cleaner - as if someone traced it recently.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: Or I have sewn two things together. I do that. Believe half of it.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: The name at the edge of the desk. You have written it.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The cut is shallower than your hand and the strokes run the wrong way for a right hand.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: Written it, not carved it. You wrote it on something else, many times, until the name stopped meaning anything to you.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: On what? Fair question. I only remember the angle of the wrist. The desk was lower than this one.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: This board had one row before.

nodes.speaker: protagonist
nodes.text: The screw holes on the second row have no rust and the paint at their rim is still sharp. It was added recently.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: When I say before, I do not mean last year. I do not give years.

nodes.speaker: voice_echo
nodes.text: And I may be remembering the one in the other building. Whether this one ever had a before, I cannot say.
